## Purpose, inputs, and scope

With the fuel estimates assembled, we'll work out which patterns the Results
should report and how to describe their uncertainty. This page draws on the
[F01 component/model record](task-f01.qmd) and
[RD04 inference and display record](task-rd04.qmd#rd04-inference-review).
The [F01](task-f01.qmd) and [RD04](task-rd04.qmd) task pages own their execution order and handoff. The shared
`sections/results.qmd` assembles the Results; RT03 maintains the shared fuel
subsection in `sections/fuel-results.qmd`.

[Results subsection in the working manuscript](draft-results.qmd#rt03-fuel-results)
reports phase-specific fuel reference means followed by the matched woody
standing-vegetation contrast. Its working allocation is 1.5–2 manuscript pages,
approximately 500 words excluding the figure, table, captions, and review note;
final pagination depends on journal formatting.

## Implemented source and review decisions

| Source or finding | Implementation in RT03 |
|---|---|
| Thesis `analysis/thesis/results.qmd`, fuel subsections | Retain the pre-PCT, post-PCT, and vegetation-transition sequence, using current publication values throughout. |
| Revised component definitions | Report woody and herbaceous vegetation separately; distinguish modeled litter and duff before PCT; omit post-PCT forest-floor estimates. |
| RD04 inference review | Use equally site-weighted, random-effect-integrated arithmetic mean loads including zeros, rather than the thesis zero-random-effect references. |
| Joint woody phase model | Report its four pre-minus-post mean reductions and covariance-aware confidence intervals, consistent with the woody load panel. Do not use the separate Student-t difference-model estimates. |
| Thesis significance and causal wording | Replace inherited p-values with descriptive treatment rankings. Report exclusion of zero only for the four computed woody-change intervals; dead-fuel phase comparisons have no paired-change tests here. |
| Slash and design interpretation | Describe potential surface-fuel contribution, not measured slash deposition; avoid attributing the entire phase transition to PCT. |
| Numerical provenance | Draw inline narrative values and the shared companion table from `rd04-fuel-model-estimates.csv`; do not carry forward the unsourced coarse-wood grand mean noted in the audit. |

**Review products:** the fuel Results draft and existing nine-panel figure and
caption. The companion [values table](draft-supplement.qmd#tbl-rd04-fuel-estimates)
is accepted for the publication supplement; its source is
`sections/rd04-fuel-estimates-table.qmd`.

**Acceptance tests:** each quantitative claim is traceable to the current
figure/CSV; point-estimate rankings are not presented as pairwise tests;
intervals describe uncertainty in means, not new-transect variation; the
standing-woody contrast is not a direct slash measure or an isolated causal
PCT effect. Scientific model acceptance and narrative review remain open.
Acceptance of the supplementary table does not mark RT03 accepted or complete.

## Implications and handoff

The RD04 CSV remains the numerical source for inline values; RT03 does not
recalculate inference or redefine its estimand. Upstream changes require a
fresh review of affected claims here. [M03](task-m03.qmd) will describe the
accepted fuel methods and [D03](task-d03.qmd) will own the management
interpretation once their queued work begins. Neither task is completed or
accepted by the narrative draft.


## Draft Results and numerical source

The hidden setup loads the shared F01 helpers and enables automatic chunk
labels before any code is displayed.

```{r}
#| label: rt03-setup
#| include: false

if (!file.exists("outputs/helpers/task-helpers.rds"))
  stop("Saved helpers are missing. Run quarto render task-f01.qmd first.")
invisible(list2env(readRDS("outputs/helpers/task-helpers.rds"), envir = knitr::knit_global()))
enable_chunk_labels()
```

The Results values need to stay aligned with the figure as the analysis develops.
We'll read the saved RD04 means and intervals and format them for inline use,
without recalculating inference. The saved formatter carries those estimates
with it and is refreshed on each render. The draft below puts the values in
context, moving from phase-specific fuel conditions to matched woody change.

```{r}
#| label: rt03-fuel-narrative-values
#| echo: true

fuel_results <- read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/tables/rd04-fuel-model-estimates.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
fuel_components <- c(
  one = "1-hour fuel",
  ten = "10-hour fuel",
  hundred = "100-hour fuel",
  coarse = "1,000-hour fuel",
  woody = "Woody vegetation",
  herb = "Herbaceous vegetation",
  litter = "Litter (pre-PCT only)",
  duff = "Duff (pre-PCT only)",
  reduction = "Woody vegetation difference (pre-PCT minus post-PCT)"
)
fuel_phases <- c(
  pre = "Pre-PCT",
  post = "Post-PCT",
  change = "Vegetation difference"
)
fuel_value <- function(
  component,
  phase,
  treatment,
  interval = FALSE,
  digits = 1L
) {
  cell <- fuel_results[
    fuel_results$component == fuel_components[[component]] &
      fuel_results$phase == fuel_phases[[phase]] &
      fuel_results$treatment == treatment,
  ]
  stopifnot(nrow(cell) == 1L)
  value <- formatC(cell$estimate, format = "f", digits = digits)
  if (interval) {
    value <- paste0(
      value,
      " (95% CI ",
      formatC(cell$lcl, format = "f", digits = digits),
      " to ",
      formatC(cell$ucl, format = "f", digits = digits),
      ")"
    )
  }
  value
}

# Save the function with the data it uses so other pages can render inline values.
environment(fuel_value) <- list2env(list(fuel_results = fuel_results,
  fuel_components = fuel_components, fuel_phases = fuel_phases), parent = baseenv())
dir.create("outputs/helpers", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(fuel_value, "outputs/helpers/fuel-value.rds")
```
